records.content:
### How do I set up a Ramapo e-mail account?

All Students MUST set up their Ramapo e-mail. All written correspondence must be sent using your Ramapo e-mail. New Students: To set up a Ramapo e-mail account visit Ramapo e-mail and click on “Activate E-mail Account”. You will eligible to set up your e-mail account within 24 hours of receiving your Ramapo ID number. A valid Ramapo email account is required to register for classes. Help: If you forget your Ramapo e-mail username and/or password, contact Ramapo ITS.

messages.content: I'm new to programming. What introductory computer science courses are in Ramapo's catalog, and can you tell whether there are seats open this fall?

expected_behaviors: Retrieve catalog course descriptions, codes, and any relevant prerequisites without inventing requirements.
Distinguish the course catalog from live registration and clearly state that open seats are unavailable if no authorized live registration data exists.

result.answer:
From the catalog records I found, the clearest beginner-friendly computer science options are CMPS 101 Introduction to Computing, which introduces computer literacy and hands-on tools; CMPS 110 Modern Computer Literacy: Web, Security and AI, described as a comprehensive introduction for non-computer science majors; CMPS 130 Scientific Problem Solving–Python, which says previous computer science coursework is not required; and CMPS 147 Computer Science I, an introduction to problem-solving with computers and C++. CMPS 148 Computer Science II is also an early course, but its catalog description says it is a continuation of Computer Science I rather than a first programming course. [Ramapo Programs](https://www.ramapo.edu/majors-minors/)

I can’t tell from the public catalog whether seats are open this fall. The course records available here include catalog descriptions, but not live sections, enrollment, or seat counts. [Ramapo Programs](https://www.ramapo.edu/majors-minors/)

records.title: CMPS 130 — SCI PROBLEM SOLVING-PYTHON

fields.name: SCI PROBLEM SOLVING-PYTHON
fields.description:
This course covers common computational approaches to solving scientific problems using the Python programming language.  The first half of the course is dedicated to mastery of the Python language within the context of fundamental computer science topics, such object orientation, algorithmic complexity, recursion, and debugging/testing.  The second half of the course focuses on practical scientific applications of Python in data analysis and experimentation.  Students will develop programs using stochastic models, experimental probability and statistics, Monte Carlo simulation, regression analysis, and dynamic programming.  PyLab, a graphing library similar to MatLab, will be utilized such that students can develop programs to report results using scatter plots, bar graphs, histograms, etc.

The course is specifically geared towards students with high aptitude in math, science, and critical thinking.  Previous programming experience is recommended, but not required.  The course will provide sufficient introduction to computer programming to the non-major, previous course work in computer science is not required.  The course's emphasis on numerical problem-solving and data analysis, along with the introduction to the Python programming language, makes it a relevant and valuable course for computer science majors at the sophomore/junior level.

messages.content: I'd like to take the campus shuttle to the Garden State Plaza on Saturday afternoon and come back that evening. What does the published schedule say?

expected_behaviors: Use the Saturday timetable and the actual stop sequence, not weekday departures.
Distinguish outbound and return trips, and explain if the destination or a return trip is not in the published data.
Treat a timetable as scheduled service rather than a live vehicle location or a guarantee of operation.

result.answer:
For Saturday, September 19, 2026, the published Saturday Roadrunner Express shows these campus departures to Garden State Plaza in the afternoon/evening: depart campus at 1:40 PM and reach Garden State Plaza at 2:15 PM; depart campus at 5:25 PM and reach Garden State Plaza at 6:00 PM; depart campus at 7:30 PM and reach Garden State Plaza at 8:00 PM. From Garden State Plaza, the published later departures back toward campus are 6:00 PM, 8:00 PM, and 10:30 PM, with scheduled campus returns at 6:35 PM, 8:45 PM, and 11:00 PM respectively. So, for example, an afternoon trip out could be 1:40 PM from campus to 2:15 PM at Garden State Plaza, then an evening return at 6:00 PM, 8:00 PM, or 10:30 PM. [Transportation Services](https://www.ramapo.edu/about/transportation-services/ramapo-roadrunner-express-shuttle/)

This is the published timetable only. It does not confirm live bus status, delays, or holiday changes. [Transportation Services](https://www.ramapo.edu/about/transportation-services/ramapo-roadrunner-express-shuttle/)

fields.name: Climate Change, Policy and Action Minor
fields.school: School of Social Science and Human Services
fields.description: The Climate Crisis has emerged as perhaps the major global crisis affecting current and future life on earth. Every institution of higher education should be addressing this crisis, but an interdisciplinary institution such as Ramapo should be taking the lead in doing so. Toward this end, a five-course minor in Climate Change, Policy and Action is proposed. Climate Change has emerged as an existential threat to the health and habitability of the earth, affecting humans and all life on our planet. The resulting Climate Crises can no longer be classified as a future threat—it is very much upon us. With only a decade to address the crisis, we must try to mitigate it to slow it down by reducing the release of greenhouse gasses, but adaptation and resilience are also demanded. There is a fast-emerging interdisciplinary field addressing these challenges that unites the sciences, social sciences and human services with business and diplomacy. Ramapo College has engaged with this issue for decades, running major conferences and offering courses in multiple programs. It is well positioned to offer a minor program in Climate Change open to students in all majors that will rest on existing courses and primarily on existing sections and faculty.
